name: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.08560 (cs.AI); v1 submitted 12 Oct 2023, v2 12 Feb 2024. DBLP: journals/corr/abs-2310-08560. DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2310.08560. No formal peer-reviewed venue is recorded; the work circulated as an arXiv technical report (its commercial successor is the Letta framework).
authors_affiliation: Charles Packer, Sarah Wooders, Kevin Lin, Vivian Fang, Shishir G. Patil, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez. Single affiliation marked '1' in the paper: University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley; Sky Computing Lab / RISELab lineage). The same team later founded Letta (formerly MemGPT).
code_url: https://research.memgpt.ai (project page redirecting to the released code/data). The original repository was github.com/cpacker/MemGPT, now github.com/letta-ai/letta (renamed/rebranded as Letta, 'formerly MemGPT'). Released artifacts: augmented MSC/DMR dataset, nested KV retrieval dataset, and embeddings for 20M Wikipedia articles.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/letta-ai/letta (continuously maintained successor framework, 'Letta, formerly MemGPT'; far more current than the frozen 2023/2024 PDF). The research-specific page is https://research.memgpt.ai.
task_domain: Long-context LLM agent / memory management. Evaluated in two domains: (1) conversational agents (multi-session chat — long-term dialogue memory, consistency, engagement) and (2) document analysis (multi-document question answering and synthetic key-value retrieval over corpora that exceed the LLM context window). Broadly a QA + interactive-agent memory-management setting.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent setting with a FROZEN, off-the-shelf LLM (no model training/fine-tuning; supervision absent). The LLM's fixed context window is treated as a constrained 'main memory' resource and is augmented with an OS-inspired hierarchical memory system. The agent is given function-call tools (via system-prompt instructions and a function schema) to self-direct paging of data between its in-context main memory and out-of-context external storage. Control flow is event-driven: events (user messages, system memory-pressure warnings, timed events) trigger LLM inference, and the LLM can chain function calls via a request_heartbeat flag. Two evaluation domains: multi-session chat (DMR consistency + conversation-opener engagement on an augmented MSC dataset) and document analysis (multi-document QA over Wikipedia + nested KV retrieval). Base LLMs are GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613), and GPT-4 Turbo (gpt-4-1106-preview).
what_is_retrieved: experiences / memories: out-of-context conversational history and stored facts (recall storage = full message history; working context = key user/persona facts), and, in document analysis, documents/passages (Wikipedia articles) and synthetic key-value records loaded into archival storage. Retrieval brings these out-of-context items back into the LLM main context via self-issued function calls (e.g. conversation/recall search, archival memory search).
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID, leaning toward a GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes. In conversational settings the retrievable store is the agent's own growing memory (recall storage of the full conversation history plus a self-edited working context), i.e. episodic memory the agent writes to during interaction. In document analysis the store is a (largely static) external corpus (e.g. a precomputed 20M-article Wikipedia embedding database, or a fixed set of synthetic KV pairs) loaded into archival storage. Both are accessed through the same self-directed function-call retrieval interface.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Top-k similarity ranking executed iteratively rather than a one-shot fixed-k cut: each retrieval function call returns paginated top-K results (vector cosine-similarity top-K), and the LLM can repeatedly page/re-query to assemble the information it needs (multi-hop collation). There is no learned ranking objective (no Recall@k/nDCG optimized) and no explicit minimal-set completeness objective; instead, function chaining + pagination lets the agent approximate complete recovery by issuing additional retrieval calls until it decides it has the answer (e.g. 'do not stop until you verify the value is not a key' in nested KV).
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: partial, Revise: no, Retain: yes]. MemGPT Retrieves out-of-context history/documents and Retains new information (writing to working context / archival / recall storage and recursive summaries). It is not a case-based-reasoning system: there is no case Reuse-via-adaptation or solution Revise step in the CBR sense. (Approximate mapping; the work is not framed as CBR.)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. MemGPT does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is framed as OS-inspired virtual context management / hierarchical memory paging.
retrieval_unit: Mixed by domain: (a) conversational message/history snippet and stored fact (a message in the FIFO queue / recall storage, or a free-text fact block in working context); (b) document/passage (a Wikipedia article retrieved by vector search in archival storage); (c) a synthetic key-value record (128-bit UUID pair) in the nested KV task. Retrieval is at the granularity of paginated database records (messages, documents, or KV entries) brought into main context.
index_source: Hybrid. Conversational recall storage is a growing, online/test-time-induced store (the full message history accumulates as the conversation proceeds, with recursive summaries written on eviction). Working context is a self-edited in-context store the agent writes online. Document-analysis archival storage is a (largely offline/precomputed) static external corpus (e.g. 20M-article Wikipedia embeddings precomputed and loaded into PostgreSQL/pgvector, or a fixed synthetic KV set).
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index over external storage. Implementation: PostgreSQL archival memory with vector search via the pgvector extension, using an HNSW index for approximate sub-second similarity queries. Recall storage holds the rolling message history (time-ordered, searchable). Main context itself is partitioned into three contiguous sections (system instructions / working context / FIFO queue), a tiered RAM-vs-disk hierarchy rather than a graph/hierarchical-category index. No knowledge graph or category->tool hierarchy.
retriever_type: Dense, off-the-shelf. Vector similarity search (cosine distance) over OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings. The same retriever is used by both MemGPT (exposed as a function the LLM can call against archival/recall storage) and the fixed-context baselines (a standard retriever-reader top-K fetch). No BM25, no learned/trained retriever; the 'retriever' in MemGPT effectively emerges from the archival-storage search function. The LLM acts as a controller that decides query terms and when to call the retriever (LLM-orchestrated retrieval over a dense index).
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The retriever uses frozen pretrained text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings with cosine-similarity vector search; it is not trained with contrastive, LM-feedback, downstream-effectiveness, RL, or value-based signals. The novelty is in how the frozen LLM self-directs (when/what to retrieve via function calls), not in learning the retriever. The base LLM is likewise not fine-tuned for MemGPT (it is prompted via system instructions).
query_construction: LLM-synthesized search queries issued as function-call arguments. The MemGPT LLM processor, guided by system-prompt instructions, formulates natural-language/keyword search queries (e.g. recall_storage.search('...'), archival memory search) based on the current situation/question, and can refine/repeat queries (paginate, reformulate) across a function-chain. In document QA the query derives from the user's question; in nested KV it is the current UUID key being looked up.
query_granularity: Step/state-level: queries are constructed dynamically at each inference cycle / function-call step as the agent reasons, not a single one-shot query at t=0. The agent issues multiple successive queries within one task (paginated / multi-hop), so retrieval is interleaved at step granularity.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / agent-initiated (self-directed). Retrieval is not on a fixed schedule; the frozen LLM decides when to call a memory-search function based on the current context and the system instructions. Function chaining (request_heartbeat=true) lets it perform multiple retrieval steps in sequence before yielding control to the user. Event-driven control flow (user/system/timed events) triggers LLM inference, after which the agent may choose to retrieve.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated request: the LLM emits a memory-retrieval function call when it judges (from system-prompt guidance and current context) that needed information is out of context. Complementary system signals shape behavior — 'memory pressure' warnings when prompt tokens exceed a warning threshold (~70% of context) and an impending FIFO-queue eviction, plus explicit instructions (e.g. 'keep searching until you verify the value is not a key'). No token-level confidence, attention-uncertainty score, learned complexity classifier, or reflection tokens.
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage (no cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker). Items are ordered purely by vector cosine similarity from the archival/recall search and returned in paginated pages; the LLM controller decides whether to page further or re-query rather than reranking results.
retrieved_context_refinement: Minimal/none as an automated post-retrieval module. Retrieved records are paginated to avoid overflowing the context window, and the LLM may iteratively page/re-query and select which results to keep in main context. There is no learned distillation, decompose-then-recompose, distractor-filtering, or compression of retrieved items; the only compression in the system is the recursive summarization applied to evicted FIFO-queue messages (a memory-management step, not a retrieval-refinement step).
tool_document_engineering: N/A. MemGPT does not index tool/skill descriptions; its function set (memory read/write/search functions) is described to the LLM via raw natural-language schemas in the system prompt, but it does not retrieve over a tool corpus.
index_content_separation: Partial / implicit. MemGPT explicitly separates a small in-context 'main memory' (system instructions + working context + FIFO queue) from heavy out-of-context content in external storage (archival + recall databases) that is loaded on demand via function calls and pagination — an OS-style RAM/disk progressive-disclosure pattern. It is not the SOP-index-then-content or lightweight-tool-index pattern of tool-retrieval works; the separation is between a fixed-size context window and unbounded external storage.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A. Not a tool-retrieval system; no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling tool registry with CRUD auto-sync. (MemGPT does use LLM function calling, but to operate its own memory functions, not to integrate a live external tool store.)
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. No inter-tool dependency modeling (no tools/APIs are retrieved).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation. Retrieved out-of-context items (messages, facts, documents, KV records) are paged into the LLM main context (prompt tokens) as text, where the frozen LLM reads them to answer or to ground its next action. The agent also self-edits its working context (writing/updating key facts) and consults working context inline. No training signal, no skill reuse, no latent-token injection — retrieved content is consumed as in-context text.
planning_integration: Inside a self-directed function-call loop (retrieve-within-a-search-loop). MemGPT interleaves retrieval with 'planning out loud' and acting: the LLM reasons, calls a memory function, reads the returned page into context, and can chain further calls (request_heartbeat=true) before yielding. This enables multi-step retrieval / multi-hop collation (e.g. nested KV lookups, collating across documents). There is no explicit task planner, MCTS, or hierarchical subtask decomposition; planning is the emergent control flow of the agentic function-chaining loop.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call within a rollout: retrieval is woven in at the granularity of individual function calls during the agent's inference cycles (the LLM can reason, call a search function, observe results, and call again), i.e. per-step/per-function-call rather than per-CoT-token or only per-final-answer.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR case-adaptation system). Retrieved content is injected as in-context text and the frozen LLM synthesizes responses from it; there is no verbatim-case-reuse-with-adaptation, execution-feedback case revision, critic-guided revision, or RL reuse-finetuning. The closest 'adaptation' is the LLM self-editing its working-context memory block over time.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw natural-language text: retrieved messages, stored fact blocks, document passages, or KV records are injected into the prompt as plain text (paginated). Working context is free-text unstructured memory the agent maintains. No executable program/skill, structured schema, or latent/soft tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mostly raw/low-abstraction units (raw message history, raw documents, raw KV records) retrieved by similarity. A higher-abstraction layer exists but is generated, not the retrieval target: recursive summaries of evicted messages and the self-curated working-context fact block (distilled key facts/preferences). So retrieval targets raw records while the agent separately maintains distilled summaries/facts in main context.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Implicit / prompt-driven only. Because MemGPT can issue multiple retrieval calls and page through results, it is robust to a noisy embedding ranking as long as the gold item is somewhere in the ranking (it can keep paging until found). System instructions (e.g. 'keep searching', 'verify the value is not a key', baselines told to reply 'INSUFFICIENT INFORMATION' / 'NO ANSWER') and an LLM-judge that requires the answer be derived from retrieved text guard against hallucination. There is no retriever-aware training, learned relevance evaluator, reason-in-documents refinement, or distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: Episodic + working/procedural memory in an OS-inspired hierarchy. Main context = system instructions (read-only) + working context (fixed-size read/write fact block) + FIFO queue (rolling message history with a recursive-summary head). External context = archival storage (read/write, arbitrary-length text, vector-searchable) + recall storage (full message-history database, searchable). Long-term, persistent, self-managed; single-agent private.
write_back: True. MemGPT self-directs writes: it stores important information from the FIFO queue into working context or archival storage on memory-pressure warnings; evicted messages are written to recall storage indefinitely; and a recursive summary is generated and stored on each queue flush. The agent also continually edits its working-context fact block.
online_growth: Yes (for conversational/recall memory). The recall-storage message history and recursive summaries grow continuously during interaction (test/deployment time), and the working context evolves. The document-analysis archival corpus (e.g. 20M-article Wikipedia, fixed synthetic KV set) is largely precomputed/static for those benchmarks, though archival storage is in principle read/write and can grow.
write_back_trigger: Multiple triggers: (1) per-step / continuous — every message and function call is appended to the FIFO queue and, once evicted, to recall storage; (2) threshold-driven memory management — when prompt tokens exceed the 'warning token count' (~70% of context) MemGPT issues a memory-pressure warning prompting the LLM to save key info to working context/archival storage, and when they exceed the 'flush token count' (~100%) the queue manager evicts a chunk and writes a new recursive summary; (3) agent-initiated — the LLM can write to working context / archival storage whenever it deems information important. Writes are NOT conditioned on task success/failure (no task reward).
failure_experience_usage: N/A in the success/failure sense: there is no task-level success/failure label, and the system does not store failed vs successful experiences contrastively or maintain failure-only corrective rules. All interaction history is stored uniformly in recall storage. (Runtime function errors, e.g. writing to a full main context, are fed back to the processor as immediate feedback within an episode, but are not persisted as labeled failure experiences for later retrieval.)
memory_evolution_update: Mixed: append-only for the message history/recall storage and archival storage (records accumulate; evicted messages stored indefinitely), with refine-overwrite dynamics for the head-of-queue recursive summary (regenerated on each flush from the prior summary + newly evicted messages) and for working context (the agent edits/overwrites its fact block as understanding evolves). FIFO eviction provides a forget-from-context (but-retain-in-recall) behavior. No dedup-merge of stored records.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/memory-management is driven by a FROZEN, prompt-instructed LLM controller plus fixed heuristic thresholds (warning/flush token counts) — not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, or trained selection policy). The decision of when/what to retrieve emerges from in-context instructions and the LLM's function-calling ability, not from training.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory: each MemGPT agent manages its own main/external context. No shared memory store or cross-agent/cross-framework experience sharing is proposed.
benchmarks: (1) Multi-session chat: an augmented version of the Multi-Session Chat (MSC) dataset (Xu et al., 2021) — Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR) consistency task (new self-instruct-generated QA over sessions 1-5 with an added session 6) and a Conversation Opener engagement task. (2) Document analysis: a multi-document question-answering task built on the 'Lost in the Middle' setup (Liu et al., 2023a) over a late-2018 Wikipedia dump (50 sampled questions), and a new Nested Key-Value (KV) retrieval task extending the synthetic KV task of Liu et al. (2023a) to multi-hop nested lookups (140 UUID pairs ~8k tokens, 0-4 nesting levels, 30 ordering configurations).
benchmark_family: memory / long-context agent (LoCoMo/LongMemEval-style long-term-conversation memory, here via augmented MSC + DMR) and QA / multi-hop (multi-document Wikipedia QA and synthetic nested key-value retrieval, i.e. 'Lost in the Middle'-derived long-context retrieval tasks). Not web/embodied/tool/code/decision-RL families.
baselines: Fixed-context (limited-context-window) versions of the same underlying LLMs: GPT-3.5 Turbo (gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, 16k), GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613, 8k), and GPT-4 Turbo (gpt-4-1106-preview, 128k), each WITHOUT MemGPT. For conversational tasks the baselines receive a lossy recursive summarization of the prior five sessions; for document QA the baselines use the same text-embedding-ada-002 retriever in a standard retriever-reader top-K setup (à la Liu et al., 2023a). A Human baseline is reported for the conversation-opener task. Truncation is shown as a context-extension comparison for document QA.
key_metrics: DMR: Accuracy (LLM-judge correctness) and ROUGE-L recall (R). Conversation opener: CSIM similarity scores to gold persona labels (SIM-1, SIM-3) and to the human-written opener (SIM-H). Document QA: accuracy (LLM-judge) as a function of effective context length / number of retrieved documents. Nested KV: accuracy as a function of nesting level (0-4).
headline_result: On the Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR) consistency task, GPT-4 + MemGPT reaches 92.5% accuracy and 0.814 ROUGE-L(R) vs 32.1% / 0.296 for the GPT-4 fixed-context baseline; GPT-4 Turbo + MemGPT reaches 93.4% / 0.827 vs 35.3% / 0.359; GPT-3.5 Turbo + MemGPT reaches 66.9% / 0.629 vs 38.7% / 0.394. MemGPT thus dramatically improves long-term-conversation consistency over fixed-context baselines (e.g. GPT-4: 32.1% -> 92.5% accuracy).
ablations: The main comparisons function as ablations of the MemGPT memory layer: with-MemGPT vs without-MemGPT (fixed-context) on the same base LLM across DMR, conversation opener, document QA, and nested KV. Findings: (a) DMR — MemGPT yields large accuracy/ROUGE gains for every base model (clear drop when MemGPT is removed); (b) Conversation opener — storing information in working context is identified as KEY to generating engaging openers; (c) Document QA — fixed-context baseline performance is capped near the retriever's single-shot quality, whereas MemGPT's iterative paged retrieval makes performance roughly invariant to context length / document count (and MemGPT often stops paging before exhausting the database); (d) Nested KV — MemGPT with GPT-4 is unaffected by nesting depth (multi-hop via repeated function queries) while all fixed-context baselines drop to 0% by 2-3 nesting levels; notably MemGPT+GPT-4 Turbo performs worse than MemGPT+GPT-4 on nested KV. No intrinsic Recall@k retrieval-only ablation.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) are not reported separately. Evaluation is end-to-end task quality (DMR accuracy/ROUGE, opener similarity, doc-QA accuracy, nested-KV accuracy). The paper discusses retriever quality qualitatively (e.g. fixed-context baselines are capped by single-shot retriever recall; MemGPT can recover the gold doc via repeated paging) but does not tabulate Recall@k.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final-answer accuracy / ROUGE / similarity). Some process-flavored signal: nested KV accuracy as a function of nesting depth reflects multi-hop reasoning quality, and document-QA accuracy vs effective context length probes whether the agent collates across retrieved pages; but there is no reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively rather than fully tabulated. MemGPT's core efficiency argument: it provides the illusion of unbounded context without paying the quadratic cost of extending the LLM context window, by paging data in/out and issuing extra retrieval calls. It can make multiple paged retriever calls (more LLM inferences/function calls than a single-shot baseline) but in practice often stops paging before exhausting the database. The pgvector HNSW index gives approximate sub-second query times. No explicit per-task token-cost, dollar-cost, or latency table comparing MemGPT vs baselines is reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Budget-capped, iterative top-K with pagination. Main context is a fixed-size resource partitioned into system instructions + fixed-size working-context block + FIFO queue; memory-pressure (~70%) and flush (~100%) token thresholds govern eviction, with a flush evicting ~50% of the context window's messages and replacing them with a recursive summary. Retrieval returns paginated top-K results; the agent pages further as needed rather than fixing a single k, and retrieval is designed to be token-aware to avoid context overflow.
benchmark_construction_and_size: DMR: self-instruct-generated memory-challenge QA pairs over the MSC dataset (each MSC conversation has 5 sessions of ~a dozen messages; a 6th single-QA session was added), with answers scored by an LLM judge against gold answers (LLM-judge correctness + ROUGE-L). Document QA: 50 questions sampled over a late-2018 Wikipedia dump; 20M-article embeddings released; LLM-judge grading requiring the answer be derived from retrieved text. Nested KV: synthetic, 140 128-bit-UUID key-value pairs (~8k tokens), nesting levels 0-4, 30 ordering configurations, answer-verifiable by exact UUID lookup. Datasets (augmented MSC/DMR, nested KV, Wikipedia embeddings) are publicly released. Difficulty signal: fixed-context GPT-4 collapses to 0% nested KV by 3 nesting levels and to ~32% DMR accuracy.
builds_on: Operating-systems virtual memory / hierarchical memory and paging (Patterson et al. 1988 — RAID/storage-tier analogy); LLM function-calling / tool-use agents (Toolformer, Schick et al. 2023; AgentBench, Liu et al. 2023b); retrieval-augmented LLMs (RAG, REALM, RETRO, Atlas/Izacard & Grave, DPR, in-context RALM); 'Lost in the Middle' long-context analysis and the synthetic KV / multi-doc QA setup (Liu et al. 2023a); ReAct-style reason-and-act 'plan out loud' (Yao et al. 2022); WebGPT pagination for context control (Nakano et al. 2021); Generative Agents memory+reflection for LLM agents (Park et al. 2023); Multi-Session Chat dataset (Xu et al. 2021); off-the-shelf OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 + PostgreSQL/pgvector/HNSW for the external store.
contrasts_with: Long-context architectures / context-window-extension approaches that pay quadratic attention cost or train longer models (sparse/efficient transformers — Longformer, Reformer, Sparse Transformers; Linformer; positional-interpolation/ALiBi context extension), and naive context-scaling — which MemGPT argues suffers diminishing returns and the 'lost in the middle' degradation; truncation/recursive-summarization fixed-context baselines that lose information; and standard single-shot retriever-reader RAG whose performance is capped by one-shot retriever recall (MemGPT instead lets the LLM iteratively page/re-query). Also distinct from Generative Agents (focuses on long-term memory of user inputs / OS-style self-managed paging rather than emergent social simulation).
lineage: Foundational work in the experience/episodic-memory + long-term-memory lineage of retrieval-augmented LLM agents (Group F: decision/memory/RL — memory-management for agents). MemGPT introduced OS-inspired tiered memory (main vs external context) with self-directed, function-call-based paging and a memory-pressure/eviction + recursive-summary control flow; it became the basis of the Letta framework and influenced many subsequent long-term-memory and agentic-memory systems (e.g. memory-augmented conversational agents, LongMemEval/LoCoMo-style memory benchmarks).
